As soon as I have access to the media, that means the authorities support me.

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your status changed in June 1991. You were elected as an MP. And from that time on, you were in a position to intervene quite a lot at the Serbian Assembly, and you published a compilation of your various speeches at the Assembly. Further on, your speeches, what you said, was broadcast by the Serb media.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You, Mr. Tomic, deliberately created a confusion between the time when the Serbian Radical Party was sending volunteers to protect Serbian villages in Slavonia before the JNA interfered in the conflict when I put myself forward as the commander of those volunteers with the time when the JNA intervened in the armed conflict and the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party went there exclusively under the command of the JNA. You deliberately made that confusion in your report and in your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please. Please wait before giving your answer, but this is indeed a fundamental question. You've listened very carefully to this question. Please answer. And let me remind you that this question is of the utmost significance, and therefore the answer should be very thought out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the spring of 1991, paramilitary units were set up by political parties, the SNO, Srpska Narodna of Jovic, Narodna Stranka is another party, and they also sent volunteers out. And then you have the Chetnik Serb movement of the Serbian Radical Party in the spring of 1991. In July of 1991, there was a session at the national Serb Assembly related to national defence matters. It was held in closed session this session, and during that session Mr. Seselj raised the issue of these paramilitary units, because some combatants had already died, casualties had been reported, and there were orphans and widows as a result of this. Therefore, at the time the question was raised of the incorporation or the integration of these paramilitary units as part of the Territorial Defence of Serbia and also of some regions located in Croatia. Therefore, you have two stages here. In a first stage volunteers are sent out by political parties. Each one of the parties is going about it in its own way, and then after the summer, after July 1991, the whole thing is reorganised. I'm talking about these volunteers being sent out in the field. And these paramilitary units were then later on incorporated in the Territorial Defence with a connection to the JNA. This is something you can find in the book related to the various speeches given by Mr. Seselj at the Serbian Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I -- just one additional question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one additional question following his answer and then we'll stop.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: After August 1992, do you have a single case where the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party went to the front line without being part of the JNA until 19 May 1992, when the JNA under the ultimatum of the Western powers who to retreat from Western Slavonia? Was there any case where we sent volunteers independently without the JNA?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After this first stage that I explained previously, but let me remind you that I am not an expert in terms of military affairs, but if you look at the documents published by the party you see that they only mention the involvement of volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party as part -- or in the ranks of the Territorial Defence and the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, we'll deal with that matter again with the expert next week. I'd like to turn to the Prosecution to ask if you have any re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time we conclude our examination of Mr. Tomic, and we would move for the admission of the exhibits that were marked for identification, including his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Thank you very much. Mr. Tomic, I would like to thank you on behalf of myself and my fellow Judges to have spent these two weeks in The Hague. I wish you a safe trip home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday you served on me, Judge, your decision that you admit into evidence the report of expert Oberschall, and in the decision it says that I do not oppose the admission. I do oppose it with my previous responses, and I also oppose this during cross-examination. Lest there occur a confusion now, I now let you know that I oppose strenuously the admission of expert Tomic as incompetent, unqualified, not objective, and very biased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. The Chamber will consider the matter, but we have to give a number, a temporary number to this report. Please can we have a number, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The expert report of Mr. Tomic will be marked for identification MFI P163.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Tomorrow we have another witness. I'm not going to give the name of the witness because protective measures have been granted. It's Witness 004. This witness will testify with protective measures, and the Chamber has decided to grant four hours to the Prosecution for the examination-in-chief, and Mr. Seselj will have four hours as well. In other words, tomorrow we'll have the examination-in-chief, and on Monday -- no, no, not on Monday but on Tuesday we'll proceed to the cross-examination stage. That's how things stand as for Witness 004. It's 7.00 p.m. Let me thank everyone here in this courtroom and I'm see you tomorrow at 8.30 a.m., 8.30 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 7th day of February, 2008, at 8.30 a.m. 23 24
